title: Calling Functions from Functions
story: A master chef doesn't do everything from scratch — they call on sous-chefs to chop vegetables, boil water, and prepare sauces. Your functions can call helper functions the same way!
why: Breaking complex tasks into smaller functions makes code readable and reusable. One function can delegate work to many others.
analogy: Functions calling functions is like a head chef delegating to sous-chefs — each person does one task, and the head chef coordinates them all.
try_it: Write a `format_name` function that calls `string.str_upper` on the last name and `string.str_lower` on the first name, then combines them with a comma.
tips: Functions can call any other function defined in the file — not just from main
Break big tasks into small functions, then have a coordinator function call them in order
Nesting calls like `f(g(x))` reads from inside out: g runs first, then f
common_mistakes: Calling a function before it's defined — define helper functions above the functions that use them
Creating functions that are too similar but not reusing them — if two functions both need to double a number, make `double` a shared helper
Over-nesting: `a(b(c(d(e(x)))))` is hard to read — use variables for clarity beyond 2 levels
